exercise.name: Push Press
aliases: Push press from the front rack

reference.title: Push Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be read at authoring time, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (dip and leg drive, then shoulder flexion and elbow extension overhead)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace before the dip, hold through the drive, breathe out as the bar passes the head or at lockout; breathe in again at the top or back on the shoulders.
breathing.cadence: Quick dip and drive, about 1.2 s down to the shoulders

prescription.tempo: Controlled dip (about 0.5 s), explosive drive, controlled lowering to the shoulders
prescription.load: Moderate to heavy; more than a strict press thanks to the leg drive
prescription.progression: Add load in small steps; push jerk and split jerk as later steps

cues.text: Bar on the front of the shoulders, hands just outside the shoulders, elbows a little in front of the bar, feet hip width, trunk tall and braced.
Dip straight down a short way by bending the knees (a quarter of a squat or less); trunk stays upright, heels down.
Drive hard up through the legs onto the balls of the feet; the bar leaves the shoulders from the leg drive.
Keep pressing: head back a little as the bar passes the face, then through under the bar.
Arms straight overhead, bar over the middle of the feet, heels back down.
Lower the bar under control back to the shoulders, softening the knees to cushion it.
Reset the brace on the shoulders before the next rep.

mistakes.fix: Keep the trunk upright; the knees bend forward, the hips go straight down.

mistakes.mistake: Dipping too deep or too slowly
mistakes.fix: Short, controlled dip, then an immediate drive.
Let the leg drive launch the bar, then press.

mistakes.mistake: Bar travelling forward around the face
mistakes.fix: Move the head back and keep the bar close to the face.

mistakes.mistake: Over-arching the lower back at lockout
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and brace the ribs down.

kinematics.setup: Rack: knees ≈5°, bar 23 cm in front of the shoulder joints
kinematics.peak: Knees ≈40°, trunk ≈6° from vertical, pelvis 4.9 cm lower
kinematics.norm: A short, upright knee bend (quarter squat or less) before the drive; dip and drive kinetics of the push press reported by Soriano 2024

kinematics.setup: From the bottom of the dip
kinematics.peak: Knees ≈5°, heels up (foot pitch 16°), bar 11.4 cm off the shoulders
kinematics.norm: Hips, knees and ankles extend explosively; heels come off the floor briefly (common coaching standard)

kinematics.peak: Overhead: upper arm ≈165° from the trunk line, elbows ≈8°, bar -1.5 cm from mid-foot
kinematics.norm: Bar from the front of the shoulders to straight arms overhead, over the middle of the feet (common coaching standard)

kinematics.setup: Overhand, 58 cm between the handle centres
kinematics.norm: Overhand, just outside the shoulders (common coaching standard)

kinematics.setup: Rack 0.8 s, dip 0.5 s, drive 0.3 s
kinematics.peak: Press 0.6 s, lockout 0.4 s, lower 1.3 s
kinematics.norm: Fast dip and drive, controlled lowering (common coaching standard)

sources.title: Soriano, Jimenez-Ormeno, Lake, McMahon, Gallo-Salazar, Mundy & Comfort 2024, kinetics and kinematics of the push press, push jerk, and split jerk (J Strength Cond Res 38(8):1359-1365)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Load is user-chosen: use a weight you can lock out with control; take the bar from a rack set at shoulder height.
Shoulder pain overhead or an over-arched lower back: lighten the load and work on mobility first.
Lower the bar to the shoulders with soft knees; do not drop it on the collarbones.
modify: Shorter dip if the knees or hips complain.
regressions: Dip-and-drive drill with an empty bar.
